questions.q: According to §2, the highest ideal of cure is:
opts: removal of the most troublesome symptom as quickly as possible
palliation of suffering until the disease runs its natural course
removal of the material cause of disease by evacuation
rapid, gentle and permanent restoration of health on easily comprehensible principles
questions.why: §2 defines the ideal cure as rapid, gentle and permanent restoration of health, or removal of the disease in its whole extent, in the shortest, most reliable and most harmless way.

questions.q: Sudden, sharp cutting neuralgic pains around the eye, worse from touch and motion, with palpitation, call for:
questions.why: Topic 2, Materia Medica. Spigelia: left-sided neuralgia, heart and eye.

questions.q: The vehicle 'sugar of milk' is preferred over cane sugar for trituration because it is:
opts: hard, gritty and only slightly soluble, which aids grinding
questions.why: Topic 3, Pharmacy. Its hardness helps subdivide the drug.

questions.q: Kent, following Swedenborg, described the vital force as:
questions.why: Kent's Lectures on Homoeopathic Philosophy call the vital force 'simple substance', an immaterial substance with formative intelligence.

questions.q: Hyperthyroidism with emaciation despite a ravenous appetite, anxiety when hungry, relief from eating and intolerance of heat, calls for:
questions.why: Iodum patients lose flesh while eating well, feel better after eating and are warm-blooded; it is used for goitre and thyrotoxicosis.

questions.q: In the 6th edition of the Organon, the 50 millesimal (LM) method of preparation is described in:
questions.why: §270 gives the LM method. §269 deals with potentisation in general and §128 with provings in the 30th potency.

questions.q: Antidiuretic hormone acts mainly on the:
questions.why: It inserts aquaporins and concentrates urine.

questions.q: A net reproduction rate (NRR) of 1 means that:
opts: each woman bears exactly one child
the population is doubling every generation
each generation of mothers is exactly replaced by an equal number of daughters
the birth rate equals 1 per 1,000 population
questions.why: NRR = 1 is replacement-level fertility, roughly equal to a TFR of about 2.1.

questions.q: An infarct in which of the following organs typically undergoes liquefactive necrosis?
questions.why: Ischaemic death of CNS tissue produces liquefactive necrosis; infarcts of other solid organs show coagulative necrosis.

questions.q: According to §§74 and 75, the most deplorable and incurable of all chronic diseases are those produced by:
questions.why: §75: artificial chronic diseases caused by allopathic treatment are the most deplorable and incurable of all.
